subject: DataBridge (PayLane) — new processor intake & evidence needed
messages:
From: Claire Horton <claire.horton@paylane.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: legal+privacy@paylane.com
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Add DataBridge as a processor for paylane-payments EU traffic

Hi Grace,

Following our conversation on Friday, PayLane needs to onboard a short-lived processor for a pilot integration: DataBridge Ltd. They will handle request routing and telemetry for a subset of EU payment flows during a two-week trial in January.

Can Redwood provide the following by EOD next Thursday so we can complete our internal compliance review?
- A current subprocessor roster that includes DataBridge once added (format that maps processing category and country).
- Evidence that DataBridge will not persist query-level payment payloads and confirmation of any caching/KV behavior.
- Any DPA addendum or minimal redline that would cover this temporary processing window (we can accept a 30-day notice window).
- Point of contact for SOC2 / encryption attestations if requested.

We expect low traffic (~1k requests/day) but it’s time-sensitive for our release. Happy to jump on a short call if that helps.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Horton
Head of Integrations, PayLane
claire.horton@paylane.com
+44 20 7123 4456

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. We can support the pilot but need to confirm a few technical and contractual items first. I’ve looped in Kimberly (Legal) and Karthik (Privacy) to prepare an intake checklist and a short DPA addendum. Jonas will coordinate capacity and routing policy.

Immediate next steps (we'll aim to get this to you by Thu EOD):
- Internal: inventory export (databridge_processor_inventory.csv) with processing categories and country tags — action: me (Grace) by Wed 5pm PT.
- Legal: draft minimal DPA addendum / redline covering the temporary window and export controls — action: Kimberly by Thu 11am PT.
- Privacy: confirm caching/KV behavior and provide a statement on retention scoping — action: Karthik by Wed EOD.
- Ops: confirm routing policy and whether requests will transit non-EU nodes — action: Jonas by Wed EOD.

Two clarifications that will speed approval: will DataBridge require any access to decrypted payloads (PII/payment tokens)? And are you requesting any telemetry snapshots for debugging that include request/response bodies?

I’ll attach the inventory CSV and a placeholder evidence bundle when ready. If you’d like a 20-minute sync, I’m free Tue 3pm PT; otherwise we’ll work asynchronously.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Add DataBridge as a processor for paylane-payments EU traffic

Thanks Grace — I reviewed the pilot spec and the preliminary inventory. A few legal points and asks before we share an addendum externally: 

1) Territorial scope & export controls: confirm which EU countries DataBridge will process for. We need country mapping in the CSV (not just "EU") so we can validate egress restrictions.

2) Caching / KV: if DataBridge uses in-memory KV for short-term routing, we need the max TTL and a guarantee that payment tokens are not persisted. If they will persist encrypted blobs for telemetry, we need details on key custody.

3) Liability & indemnity carveout: because this is an experimental integration, Legal recommends a limited liability threshold and a 30-day notice plus a one-time renewal clause. I’ve prepared a minimal redline (attached) that preserves Redwood’s standard DPA protections but shortens notice and adds an escrow-style onshore fallback if DataBridge is unreachable.

4) Evidence: ask SOC2 type II report (if available) or alternatively a self-attestation + technical architecture diagram. Also request TLS mutual-auth details and KMS provider for any key storage.

If we can get the country list and an ops confirmation on caching by EOD Wed, I can send the redline to PayLane legal Thu morning. I attached: dpa_addendum_redline.pdf (stub) and a one-page guidance note for vendors.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Claire — attaching the requested items and proposed next steps. Please see inline summary and attachments.

Summary: 
- Inventory: databridge_processor_inventory.csv (attached) — contains country-level mapping: Ireland, Germany, France, Netherlands.
- Caching: Ops (Jonas) confirmed DataBridge will use ephemeral in-memory routing cache with TTL=45s; no persistence of payment tokens. Statement included in evidence_package.zip.
- DPA addendum: Kimberly's minimal redline attached (dpa_addendum_redline.pdf) — this shortens notice to 30 days and includes the onshore fallback clause for emergency routing.
- Evidence: included evidence_package.zip contains vendor attestation, architecture diagram, and TLS/KMS notes. SOC2 is not available for DataBridge; they provided a self-attestation and pen-test summary.

Next steps / timeline:
- Thu 11am PT: Redwood legal will send the redline to PayLane legal for quick review (link to redline attached).
- Fri EOD: Target to finalize signatures (DocuSign link below).
- Jan pilot window: We will implement routing rules to scope traffic to the agreed country list only; operator logs will be retained 7 days.
